topics.title: Area and Perimeter of Plane Figures
topics.concept:
What is Mensuration?

Mensuration is the branch of mathematics that deals with the measurement of geometric figures — their lengths, areas, and volumes. It helps us quantify the space occupied by 2D shapes and 3D solids.

Key Definitions:

  • Perimeter: The total distance around the boundary of a 2D shape
  • Area: The amount of surface enclosed within a 2D shape (square units)

Formulas for Common 2D Shapes:

ShapePerimeterArea
**Rectangle** (length = l, breadth = b)\(2(l + b)\)\(l \times b\)
**Triangle** (base = b, height = h)\(a + b + c\)\(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\)
**Triangle** (using Heron's formula)\(a + b + c\)\(\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\)
**Circle** (radius = r)\(2\pi r\) (circumference)\(\pi r^2\)

Heron's Formula Details:

For a triangle with sides a, b, c:

  • Semi-perimeter: \(s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}\)
  • Area = \(\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\)

What is Mensuration? Mensuration is the branch of mathematics that deals with the measurement of geometric figures — their lengths, areas, and volumes. It helps us quantify the space occupied by 2D shapes and 3D solids.

Key Definitions: - Perimeter: The total distance around the boundary of a 2D shape - Area: The amount of surface enclosed within a 2D shape (square units)

Formulas for Common 2D Shapes:

ShapePerimeterArea
Square (side = s)\(4s\)\(s^2\)
Rectangle (length = l, breadth = b)\(2(l + b)\)\(l \times b\)
Triangle (base = b, height = h)\(a + b + c\)\(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\)
Triangle (using Heron's formula)\(a + b + c\)\(\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\)
Circle (radius = r)\(2\pi r\) (circumference)\(\pi r^2\)

Heron's Formula Details: For a triangle with sides a, b, c: - Semi-perimeter: \(s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}\) - Area = \(\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\)

SQUARE AND RECTANGLE:

    Square (side = s):          Rectangle (l, b):
    
        ┌─────┐                     ┌─────────┐
        │     │                     │         │
        │  s  │                     │    b    │
        │     │                     │         │
        └─────┘                     └─────────┘
            s                            l
    
    Perimeter = 4s                 Perimeter = 2(l+b)
    Area = s²                      Area = l × b


TRIANGLE (base × height):

                     /\
                    /  \
                   /    \
                  /      \
            h    /        \
                /          \
               /____________\
                     b
    
    Area = ½ × b × h


CIRCLE:

                    ┌─────┐
                  ╱       ╲
                 │    r    │
                 │    ●    │
                  ╲       ╱
                    └─────┘
    
    Circumference = 2πr  (or πd, where d=2r)
    Area = πr²


HERON'S FORMULA - TRIANGLE WITH THREE SIDES:

    Triangle with sides a, b, c:
    
                A
               /\
              /  \
            c/    \b
            /      \
           /________\

Area: space inside a 2D shape (square units)
Triangle: A=½×b×h, or Heron's formula if height unknown
Heron's formula: use when three sides are known

topics.title: Surface Area and Volume of Cube and Cuboid
topics.concept:
What are 3D Solids?

Three-dimensional (3D) solids have length, breadth (width), and height. They occupy space.

Definitions:

  • Surface Area: The total area of all faces of a 3D solid (square units)
  • Lateral Surface Area (LSA): Area of only the side faces (excluding top and bottom)
  • Total Surface Area (TSA): Area of all faces including top and bottom
  • Volume: The amount of space inside a 3D solid (cubic units)

Cube (all sides equal = a):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(6a^2\)
Volume\(a^3\)

Cuboid (length = l, breadth = b, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2(lb + bh + hl)\)
Volume\(l \times b \times h\)

sections.content:
What are 3D Solids? Three-dimensional (3D) solids have length, breadth (width), and height. They occupy space.

Definitions: - Surface Area: The total area of all faces of a 3D solid (square units) - Lateral Surface Area (LSA): Area of only the side faces (excluding top and bottom) - Total Surface Area (TSA): Area of all faces including top and bottom - Volume: The amount of space inside a 3D solid (cubic units)

Cube (all sides equal = a):

MeasurementFormula
Lateral Surface Area (LSA)\(4a^2\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(6a^2\)
Volume\(a^3\)

Cuboid (length = l, breadth = b, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Lateral Surface Area (LSA)\(2h(l + b)\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2(lb + bh + hl)\)
Volume\(l \times b \times h\)

CUBE (a = side):

        ┌─────────┐
       /│        /│
      / │       / │
     /  │      /  │
    └───┼─────┘   │
    │   │     │   │
    │  ┌───────┼───┘
    │ /       │ /
    │/        │/
    └─────────┘
    
    All 6 faces are squares of side a
    LSA = 4a² (4 side faces)
    TSA = 6a² (all 6 faces)
    Volume = a³


CUBOID (l, b, h):

        ┌──────────┐
       /│         /│
      / │        / │
     /  │       /  │ h
    └───┼──────┘   │
    │   │      │   │
    │  ┌───────┼───┘
    │ /   b    │ /
    │/         │/
    └──────────┘
         l
    
    TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) [3 pairs of identical faces]
    LSA = 2h(l + b) [4 side faces]
    Volume = l × b × h


VISUALIZING VOLUME - CUBE:

    1 cm³ cube:
    ┌─┐
    │ │ 1 cm
    └─┘
     1 cm
    
    Volume = 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm = 1 cm³


COMPARING CUBE AND CUBOID:

    Feature           Cube               Cuboid
    ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    All edges         Equal              Not equal
    Faces             6 squares          6 rectangles
    TSA               6a²                2(lb+bh+hl)
    Volume            a³                 l×b×h


REAL-LIFE EXAMPLES:

    Cube:           Rubik's cube,

points: Cube: all edges equal (a); Cuboid: l, b, h (may be different)
LSA = area of side faces only (no top/bottom)
TSA = LSA + area of top and bottom

topics.title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinder and Cone
topics.concept:
What are Cylinder and Cone?

  • Cylinder: A 3D solid with two parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface
  • Cone: A 3D solid with a circular base and a curved surface tapering to a point (vertex)

Right Circular Cylinder (radius = r, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2\pi r(r + h)\)
Volume\(\pi r^2 h\)

Right Circular Cone (radius = r, height = h, slant height = l):

MeasurementFormula
Curved Surface Area (CSA)\(\pi r l\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(\pi r(r + l)\)
Volume\(\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h\)

Important Notes:

  • π ≈ 3.14 or 22/7
  • CSA is also called lateral surface area
  • For cone, l (slant height) is NOT the same as h (vertical height)

sections.content:
What are Cylinder and Cone? - Cylinder: A 3D solid with two parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface - Cone: A 3D solid with a circular base and a curved surface tapering to a point (vertex)

Right Circular Cylinder (radius = r, height = h):

MeasurementFormula
Curved Surface Area (CSA)\(2\pi rh\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(2\pi r(r + h)\)
Volume\(\pi r^2 h\)

Right Circular Cone (radius = r, height = h, slant height = l):

MeasurementFormula
Slant Height (l)\(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\)
Curved Surface Area (CSA)\(\pi r l\)
Total Surface Area (TSA)\(\pi r(r + l)\)
Volume\(\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h\)

Important Notes: - π ≈ 3.14 or 22/7 - CSA is also called lateral surface area - For cone, l (slant height) is NOT the same as h (vertical height)

RIGHT CIRCULAR CYLINDER:

         ┌───┐
        /    │
       │  r  │
        \    │ h
         └───┘
    
    CSA (curved surface) = 2πrh (label around)
    TSA = 2πr(r + h) (CSA + two circular ends)
    Volume = πr²h


RIGHT CIRCULAR CONE:

           /\
          /  \
         /    \
        /      \ l
       /        \
      /          \
     └────────────┘
           r
    
    Slant height l = √(r² + h²)
    CSA = πrl (curved part only)
    TSA = πr(r + l) (CSA + circular base)
    Volume = (1/3)πr²h


CYLINDER VS CONE - VISUAL COMPARISON:

    Cylinder:                     Cone:
    
     ┌─────────┐                  ╱╲
    ╱           ╲                ╱  ╲
   │             │              ╱    ╲
   │             │             ╱      ╲
   │             │            ╱        ╲
   │             │           ╱          ╲
    ╲           ╱           └────────────┘
     └─────────┘
    
    Volume = πr²h              Volume = (1/3)πr²h
    
    Cone has exactly 1/3 the volume of a cylinder
    with same base radius and height!


REAL-LIFE EXAMPLES:

    Cylinder:   Soda can, water tank, pipe, candle
    Cone:       Ice cream cone, party hat, funnel, traffic cone

points: Cone CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(r+l), Volume = (1/3)πr²h
A cone has 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with same base and height
Always use consistent units for all measurements
